title: The Arrow Matrix
subtitle: how thousands of sliders step at once
name: ModelInMotion_LogisticFE_E08_TheArrowMatrix
status: DRAFT: script under review together with its animatic.

segments.visual: Episode 7's map: the staircase of 54 rounds, then the straight path of five steps.

sentences.text: Last time, taking turns took 54 rounds.
sentences.say: Last time, taking turns took fifty-four rounds.

sentences.text: And we ended on a promise: let the sliders and the dial step together, and it takes five.

segments.visual: Episode 6's machine in miniature: Dune's slider moves, and the dial's meter moves with it.

sentences.text: But stepping together is harder than it sounds.
When Dune's slider moved, two episodes ago, the dial's meter moved too.
To step together, every control has to know how its move disturbs every meter.

segments.visual: A small 6 × 6 grid beside a vast one: 5 clinics, then 7,000 providers and 50 million cells.

sentences.text: For five clinics, that is a small table. For 7,000 providers, it is 50 million numbers.
sentences.say: For five clinics, that is a small table. For seven thousand providers, it is fifty million numbers.

sentences.text: So how can this possibly be fast?

segments.visual: Series logo and wordmark; arc and episode title.

sentences.text: Welcome back to Model in Motion.
Today: the arrow matrix.

segments.visual: An empty 6 × 6 table. Rows are the six meters, columns the six controls: five clinics and the dial.

sentences.text: Here is that table for our five clinics, at the fit. One row for each meter, one column for each control.
Each cell says how much that meter moves when that control does.

segments.visual: The diagonal fills in: 6.38, 6.66, 3.82, 2.31, 0.02. Then the corner: 10.20.

sentences.text: Down the diagonal is each clinic's own wobble, from last time: 6.38 for Alder, 6.66 for Birch, down to 0.02 for Elm.
sentences.say: Down the diagonal is each clinic's own wobble, from last time: six point three eight for Alder, six point six six for Birch, down to zero point zero two for Elm.

sentences.text: In the corner is the dial's own: 10.2.
sentences.say: In the corner is the dial's own: ten point two.

segments.visual: The last row and last column fill in: 0.97, 5.94, 2.35, 0.93, 0.

sentences.text: Along the two edges is how strongly each clinic is tied to the dial.
Birch, with 24 higher-risk patients, most of all: 5.94. Elm, with none: zero.
sentences.say: Birch, with twenty-four higher-risk patients, most of all: five point nine four. Elm, with none: zero.

segments.visual: The twenty remaining cells show as empty. One is picked out: Alder's slider, Birch's meter. Then an outline traces the arrowhead.

sentences.text: And everywhere else, nothing. Alder's slider cannot move Birch's meter, because no patient belongs to both.
That is not an approximation. It is the model.
Look at the shape it leaves: an arrowhead.

segments.visual: A square for the crowd's table, drawn as an arrow: 40,804 cells, 1,004 not zero.

sentences.text: With five clinics, the shape hardly matters. So scale up.
Our crowd of 200 providers, with two risk factors, has a table of 40,804 cells. Only 1,004 of them are not zero.
sentences.say: Our crowd of two hundred providers, with two risk factors, has a table of forty thousand eight hundred and four cells. Only one thousand and four of them are not zero.

segments.visual: A larger square: 7,000 providers, 50 risk factors, 49,702,500 cells, 1.4% not zero.

sentences.text: A national measure, with 7,000 providers and 50 risk factors, has almost 50 million cells. Nearly all of them are empty.
sentences.say: A national measure, with seven thousand providers and fifty risk factors, has almost fifty million cells. Nearly all of them are empty.

sentences.text: Treat that as an ordinary table, and you are stuck. Use the arrow, and it is easy.

segments.visual: The 6 × 6 table again. One clinic's three cells are picked out: its diagonal cell and its two edge cells.

sentences.text: Here is how. Take one clinic at a time.
Square its tie to the dial, divide by its own wobble, and take that away from the corner.

segments.visual: Clinic by clinic, a small amount leaves the corner: 0.15, 5.30, 1.45, 0.38, 0. The corner counts down from 10.20 to 2.93.

sentences.text: Alder takes away 0.15. Birch, 5.30. Cedar, 1.45. Dune, 0.38. Elm, nothing.
sentences.say: Alder takes away zero point one five. Birch, five point three zero. Cedar, one point four five. Dune, zero point three eight. Elm, nothing.

sentences.text: The corner falls from 10.2 to 2.93.
sentences.say: The corner falls from ten point two to two point nine three.

segments.visual: The clinic rows and columns dim. Only the corner cell stays lit: 2.93.

sentences.text: And now the sliders are out of the problem. What is left is one small number, for the dial alone.

segments.visual: The same 2.93 built another way: 0.82 + 0.64 + 0.90 + 0.56 + 0, one piece per clinic.

sentences.text: That number has a meaning. It adds up, clinic by clinic, how much patients differ in risk from others in their own clinic.
Elm, where every patient is lower-risk, adds nothing. It is Episode 4's idea again: the risk rule is learned inside clinics.
sentences.say: Elm, where every patient is lower-risk, adds nothing. It is Episode four's idea again: the risk rule is learned inside clinics.

segments.visual: Two bars: 10.20 before folding, 2.93 after. A label: 3.5 times.

sentences.text: It is also a warning. Ignore the clinics, and the data would seem to say three and a half times as much about the dial as they really do.

segments.visual: The machine at the plain guess. Beside the dial: its first step, 1.81.

sentences.text: So the dial's step takes one division. From the plain guess, it is 1.81.
sentences.say: So the dial's step takes one division. From the plain guess, it is one point eight one.

sentences.text: Then each clinic takes its own step, corrected for what the dial just did.

segments.visual: Sliders and dial move at once. A step counter: 1, 2, 3, then 5. The meters level.

sentences.text: Watch the machine. One joint step, and the dial reads 1.81. A second: 2.00. A third: 2.0164, the top.
sentences.say: Watch the machine. One joint step, and the dial reads one point eight one. A second: two point zero zero. A third: two point zero one six four, the top.

sentences.text: Five steps until the dial stops moving, where taking turns needed 54.
sentences.say: Five steps until the dial stops moving, where taking turns needed fifty-four.

segments.visual: Three rows: the risk factor recorded as 0 and 1, as 5 and 6, as 50 and 51. Five steps each time.

sentences.text: And the trouble with where we put zero? Record the risk factor five units higher, or fifty. The joint path does not change at all.

segments.visual: Three jobs in a row: add up over patients, fold once per provider, solve one small system. Then a test: 2,000 providers, 205,367 patients, under a second.

sentences.text: Each step is three cheap jobs: add up over the patients, fold once for each provider, and solve one small system.
We tried it on 2,000 providers and about 200,000 patients. The fit took well under a second.
sentences.say: We tried it on two thousand providers and about two hundred thousand patients. The fit took well under a second.

segments.visual: The same data as an ordinary table: 2,002 columns wide, 3.3 gigabytes.

sentences.text: Written out as an ordinary table, with a column for every provider, the same data would fill 3.3 gigabytes before any fitting began.
sentences.say: Written out as an ordinary table, with a column for every provider, the same data would fill three point three gigabytes before any fitting began.

segments.visual: A caution card: one patient, one provider. A second grouping drawn across the first, and the empty cells fill in.

sentences.text: So a separate number for every provider is not a computing problem. It only looked like one.
One caution. The arrow needs every patient to belong to exactly one provider. A second grouping that cuts across the first would break it.

segments.visual: Three recap cards, each with a small icon.

sentences.text: Let's gather it up.
Clinics disturb each other only through the dial, so the table is an arrow.
Fold each clinic into the corner, and one small system is left.
Nothing is approximated. It is last episode's step, taken for everything at once.

segments.visual: The folded number, 2.93, large; the next episode's title.

sentences.text: And keep an eye on that folded number, 2.93. It says how firmly the data hold the dial in place.
sentences.say: And keep an eye on that folded number, two point nine three. It says how firmly the data hold the dial in place.

sentences.text: Next time: how sure are we?

segments.visual: Series end card with the next episode title.

sentences.text: This has been Model in Motion. Thanks for following the story.
